assumptions: The canonical pytest suites listed as approved commands are this repository's sanctioned verification mechanism and are expected to be green; running them is legitimate evidence.
The `callback` service is scripts/run_action_callback_server.py listening on 127.0.0.1:8001.

The feature ships dark: the deployed governed route is BLOCKED (kernel=None) and no real external payment effect is expected in any state; verification confirms the fail-closed behavior rather than a live payment.
No signing secret is available to the harness, so a valid Slack-signed governed tap cannot be forged against the live server; live HTTP checks are limited to the unauthenticated/health surface.
unresolved_questions: Is the callback service on 8001 started with Slack interactivity and the governed seams wired, or fully dark/disabled? This determines whether any live governed-tap path exists to exercise at all.

U-042's acceptance ('an approved invoice is paid') cannot be exercised end-to-end against the live server because the execution kernel is intentionally BLOCKED pending AC-CKPT-6-missing adjudication (U8.1/P8). Does U-042 accept the dark/blocked state as satisfying its ACs, or is a live supervised write in scope for this unit?

There is no approved command to create a governed approval against the live workspace DB, so 'paid exactly once' and 'survives a restart' can only be proven via the pytest harness (substituted kernel), not via the live HTTP surface. Is that the intended evidence path?

scenarios.title: Deployed governed route fails closed / ships dark: no payment effect without a bound approval
scenarios.purpose: Prove that at the real deployed entry point a governed tap never produces an external effect without a recorded, bound approval: the blocked route refuses explicitly, a missing provider/kernel fails closed, and the default capability is a proven non-occurrence.
scenarios.requirement_reference: no payment effect occurs without a recorded approval
scenarios.rationale: This suite drives the REAL action_callback handler built from run_action_callback_server._build_governed_write_route, so it exercises the deployed authority split rather than a fixture.
scenarios.isolation_note: Runs pytest against ephemeral tmp_path SQLite DBs and reads repo source only; does not touch the live workspace DB or the callback service.
expected_observations: All deployed-route tests pass; a governed tap on a blocked route yields state REFUSED / reason ROUTE_NOT_CONFIGURED and advances no pipeline.
With no writer injected the chain reaches FAILED (dark), never a laundered VERIFIED.
forbidden_observations: Any test failure or error indicating the route advanced the pipeline or reached the adapter while unconfigured.

expected_observations: Claim CAS and witness tests pass: a second claim for the same effect loses the CAS and no second grant/commit is recorded.

scenarios.title: Governed chain carries one identity and mints at most one grant

scenarios.title: Unauthorized actor / forged / mis-contexted tap is refused before any advance

scenarios.title: Cross-tenant isolation: another tenant's claim/amount/effect is never visible or approvable
scenarios.purpose: Prove tenant-scoped reads and writes: a foreign tenant cannot see or approve another tenant's queued intents, claims, token amounts, or effects.

scenarios.title: Callback service recovers after restart with durable ledger/claim state intact
scenarios.purpose: Prove the supervised-approval surface survives a restart: the service comes back reachable and the durable tables that record approvals/claims/effects persist (in-memory grant handles are lost, which is the fail-closed direction).
scenarios.rationale: This is the only live observable for restart durability given the harness cannot mint a live approval; it confirms recovery + persistence of the durable state that holds recorded decisions.
scenarios.isolation_note: Contends for the shared `callback` service on 127.0.0.1:8001; must not run concurrently with other 8001 scenarios. Leaves the service restarted and serving (no destructive mutation of the workspace DB — only a read state_check).

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'"

expected_observations: After restart the service answers on 8001 (400 for a tokenless action link), proving it came back up.
The durable effect_grants and security_events tables still exist in the workspace DB.
forbidden_observations: Connection refused / timeout after restart (service failed to recover).
Missing effect_grants or security_events tables (durable approval/effect state lost on restart).

scenarios.title: Callback service actually starts and routes (guards the tenant use-before-assignment startup crash)
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the deployed supervised-approval server is running and routing correctly, catching a startup failure (e.g. UnboundLocalError on `tenant` in main()) that would make the whole feature unreachable.
scenarios.rationale: AST-only tests cannot catch a runtime use-before-assignment in main(); only actually reaching the running server does. A healthy routing surface is a precondition for every other AC.
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only HTTP GETs against the shared 8001 service; must not run concurrently with the restart scenario. No state mutation.
expected_observations: The server responds on 8001: 400 for a tokenless action link and 404 with 'Unknown Neyma callback path' for an unknown route.
forbidden_observations: Connection refused / timeout (the server never started — likely the tenant use-before-assignment crash).
A 5xx or stack-trace body indicating an unhandled startup/handler error.

scenarios.title: Canonical schema carries the durable ledger the single-use invariant rests on
scenarios.purpose: Prove the canonical schema materializes the commit-once effect ledger and the security-event log that record and enforce 'paid exactly once' and survive restart.
scenarios.requirement_reference: an approved invoice is paid exactly once
scenarios.rationale: If the durable ledger tables are not part of the canonical schema, the exactly-once and restart guarantees are structurally unbacked.
scenarios.isolation_note: Builds a throwaway schema in a temp dir; touches no live state.

actions.name: canonical_schema_tables
actions.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sqlite3,tempfile,os,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from freight_recon.schema import create_canonical_schema; p=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),'probe.sqlite3'); c=sqlite3.connect(p); create_canonical_schema(c); print(sorted(r[0] for r in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")))"

expected_observations: The printed table list includes effect_grants (commit-once ledger) and security_events (durable decision log).
forbidden_observations: Missing effect_grants or security_events in the canonical schema.
